title: South Korea's Lee says AI appears to have been used in bank hacks
source_used: Reuters text as carried by The Economic Times (m.economictimes.com AMP copy); context from The Korea Times (Yonhap) report of the same cabinet meeting
key_facts: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said on Tuesday 6 Oct 2026 that AI models are believed to have been used in some recent hacking incidents against banks.

Speaking at a cabinet meeting, he said signs of AI being used had emerged, causing considerable public concern, and asked officials to establish the circumstances swiftly and concentrate personnel and resources on minimising the damage.
He called for the country to develop cybersecurity methods suited to the AI era.

Police have launched a full-scale investigation into the attacks on commercial banks that led to a breach of customers' personal information (Yonhap, cited by Reuters); the Korea Times says a 28-member police team is on the case.
Shinhan Bank and KB Kookmin Bank had reported cyberattacks, the Financial Services Commission said on Friday; Yonhap reported that Hana Bank and Woori Bank also suffered breaches.
Authorities have not yet disclosed what kind of AI tools were used or the full scale of the breaches.
On Sunday 4 Oct, FSC Chairman Lee Eog-weon convened an emergency meeting and warned the sector to respond with the highest level of vigilance.
quote_evidence: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said on Tuesday that AI models are believed to have been used in some recent hacking incidents against banks and called for the country to develop cybersecurity methods suited to the AI era.
"In some hacking incidents, signs have emerged of AI being used, causing considerable public concern and anxiety," Lee said during a cabinet meeting.
Authorities have not yet disclosed details on what kind of AI tools were used in the hacking incidents or the full scale of the breaches.
why_it_matters_hint: The head of state links AI to attacks on several banks, which raises pressure on regulators and banks, but no AI tools or breach size have been disclosed.
event_date: 6 Oct 2026 (cabinet meeting); the bank hacks were first reported 2 to 3 Oct 2026
notes: Reuters page returned HTTP 401, so the Reuters text was read on The Economic Times copy; the entry url stays the Reuters original. Follow-up of our 4 Oct 2026 item (Lee orders a full investigation) and 5 Oct 2026 item (seven firms hit). Same story line as C12-09 and C12-14.
